newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades mostly steady.

text.p: German call money rates traded mostly steady on Friday, failing to dip further as liquidity conditions appeared less ample than in previous days.

Overnight funds traded between 3.00 to 3.04 percent during the session with the bulk of funds changing hands between 3.02/3.03 percent, dealers said. On Thursday, funds traded mostly around 3.00 percent.

"Things were still mostly in equilibrium, but the reason we did trade consistently at the 3.00 percent level was that the holdings at the Bundesbank fell off slightly," one dealer said. But the shortage poses no real problems, dealers added.
"We are missing about two billion marks in our reserve holdings, but that is not so much of a problem because banks more than fulfilled the requirements in the past days," another trader said.

On Thursday, banks held 38.4 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank, down from 40.4 billion marks held one day earlier. Average monthly reserves also dipped to 42.1 billion marks from 43.0 billion marks.
Dealers said they were pleased the Bundesbank had clearly decided to move the money market away from Lombard borrowings.
But they also said that this did not indicate the Bundesbank was planning to alter its repo rate, something Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing had also confirmed at a conference here.
Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rates were at 3.05067 percent on Friday after 3.04667 percent on Thursday.
